review_notes: I reviewed the whole 30-line file. It has one theorem. The only repetition is the three steps that prove hs, hr and ht. Each one has the same shape: `have h : (k : R) * x = 0 := by linear_combination …` followed by `exact hk.mul_right_eq_zero.mp h`. The three linear combinations are different, and each is a one-line calculation. The unit-cancellation step is a single call to existing API. A shared helper would only wrap `IsUnit.mul_right_eq_zero`, which is the kind of thin wrapper the rubric excludes. It would also add a declaration for fewer lines than it saves. The repetition is also within one proof, not across two proofs. I did not look for other files that repeat this argument, because the rubric needs nontrivial repeated reasoning and this proof has none.
